findings.description: README and ADR 32 say a re-scaffold moves the emitted workflow's claude-code-action pin, but plan.utils.ts never overwrites an existing .github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml, so a re-scaffold leaves the pin where it was.
findings.body:
**A re-scaffold doesn't move the action pin. The new README paragraph and ADR 32 both say it does.**

The README now says: "A re-scaffold moves it too. To follow Claude Code between re-scaffolds, let Dependabot bump the workflow's actions." ADR 32 builds its decision to emit no `dependabot.yml` on the same idea: "A scaffolded repository keeps its pin until it re-scaffolds". Its cost-accepted line, "a repository that does neither…", treats a re-scaffold as the fallback.

The scaffolder skips the workflow when the file already exists:

```ts
} else if (existsSync(abs(target))) {
  actions.push({ kind: "skip", target, reason: "already present; never overwritten" });
```
([src/plan.utils.ts:296-297](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/agentspine/blob/015a3f3d3f0a42b4bf8b131113de4f8c16da9ef8/src/plan.utils.ts#L292-L302))

Nothing else rewrites the file:

- `apply.utils.ts:96-103` keeps a target that already exists.
- `--force` only bypasses the dirty-tree check.
- No other code path writes this workflow.

Running `npx agentspine` again therefore leaves both the `claude-code-action` pin and `AGENTSPINE_VERSION` unchanged. The only sign is a `skip` line. A user who re-scaffolds to get a newer Claude Code keeps reviewing on the old one, which is the silent degradation `AGENTS.md` names as this project's failure mode.

The sentence "Re-scaffold to move that pin." (README line 140, from v0.1.0) has the same flaw. This PR extends it to the Claude Code version and rests a new decision on it.

Possible fix:

- Say that a re-scaffold moves neither pin unless the workflow is deleted first. Then Dependabot, or a manual edit, is the only way to move the pin.
- Revisit ADR 32's rationale and its cost-accepted line to match.

- [README.md#L142-L146](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/agentspine/blob/015a3f3d3f0a42b4bf8b131113de4f8c16da9ef8/README.md#L142-L146)
- [docs/design/0001-architecture.md#L935-L940](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/agentspine/blob/015a3f3d3f0a42b4bf8b131113de4f8c16da9ef8/docs/design/0001-architecture.md#L935-L940)

findings.description: README hard-codes "v1.0.251, Claude Code 2.1.301" next to advice to let Dependabot bump the action daily, so the first merged bump makes the claim stale; the matrix hedges it as "checked against", the README doesn't.

The permission lock's "agent mode passes no --permission-mode" fact is still cited at claude-code-action v1.0.237 (fd1c128) while the pin moved to v1.0.251; the PR re-checked SENSITIVE_PATHS and the SDK version but not this, so the cite is stale (managed deny rules still hold either way).

The new claim that claude-code-action v1.0.251's bun.lock pins claude-agent-sdk 0.3.301 (Claude Code 2.1.301) cites no file line or commit SHA, though AGENTS.md asks tool-source facts to cite file and line (decision 32 does so for dependabot-core).

Decision 32 says "The template now bumps its pinned actions daily with Dependabot (its #35-#40)" without saying "the template" is the upstream repository (the same decision uses "the template the ci-review pack emits" for templates/), so this line, and "The template is still on upload-artifact v4" and "differs from the template", read as contradicting the PR's own templates/ changes.

The new test splits on "uses: actions/setup-node@" and cuts each chunk at the next "\n\s+- ", so a list inside a step's with: block ends the chunk early, and a package-manager-cache: false in a comment would count as set.
The new test's title says "in every job", but it checks every setup-node step: a job that lost its setup-node step would still pass, since the >0 guard is per file.
The new describe.each repeats the [template, repo copy] table a third time (also at lines 56-59 and 103-106); hoisting it to one const would make covering another file a single edit.

"Re-scaffold to move that pin" (README, since v0.1.0), ADR 23 and the template's "moves only when you re-scaffold" comment all assume a re-scaffold rewrites the workflow, but plan.utils.ts skips an existing one, so the agentspine tooling pin never moves that way either.

refuted_findings.description: The ADR says "The template is still on `upload-artifact` v4", but this PR moves the template to v7 at three sites.
refuted_findings.refutation: Across decisions 28-32, "the template" means the upstream repository this repo ports from: "Template #16" (line 888), "its #35-#40" (917), "as the template's does" (933). Line 945's "It moves here" sets that upstream against this repo, so the sentence makes no claim about templates/. At most this is the wording nit recorded at line 917.

refuted_findings.description: The ADR ends with "This differs from the template, which caches its own tooling's lockfile on purpose", but this PR sets `package-manager-cache: false` in the template's `setup-node` steps too.
refuted_findings.refutation: "Its own tooling's lockfile" refers to the upstream template repository, which has tooling of its own. The emitted templates/ workflow runs in the user's checkout and has no lockfile of its own. Line 952 of the ADR already says every setup-node step in the emitted workflow turns the cache off, so nothing contradicts the PR. At most this is a wording nit.

process_issues.description: .claude-pr/ held only CLAUDE.md. The PR's copies of the RESTORE_PATHS entries (AGENTS.md, templates/github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml) were missing, so reviewers read them through `git show HEAD:<path>` instead.
A combined read-only command and a standalone `git ls-tree` needed approval and did not run. The reviewer got the same information another way.

Without the Dependabot docs, the reviewer guessed that a `/templates/github/workflows` directory might not be scanned. That contradicts the dependabot-core source ADR 32 cites, and the mechanism was unproven, so the finding was dropped.

permission_denials.input: git grep -n "actions/\|uses:" HEAD -- templates ':!templates/github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml' | head; git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD templates/github; git show HEAD:templates/github/workflows
